hooks.statusMessage: Run tests after change (returns failures to the agent)

hooks.command:
in=$(cat); if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE '"stop_hook_active": ?true'; then code=1; else code=2; fi; out=$(printf '%s' "$in" | dotnet test 2>&1) || { [ "$code" = 2 ] || printf '%s
' 'Still failing after the agent was sent back once; not blocking again this turn.' >&2; printf '%s
' "$out" >&2; exit $code; }; [ -z "$out" ] || printf '%s
' "$out"
hooks.statusMessage: Tests must pass: All tests in the affected projects pass.

hooks.prompt:
Claude has finished a turn and wants to stop. These Iron Laws bind its work:

- Never Fake Verification: Never claim code works, compiles, or passes tests without actually running the verification and reading its output.

Answer {"ok": true} unless the transcript shows the work of this turn breaking one of these laws. Then answer {"ok": false, "reason": "<law>: what was done, and what to correct"}. Unfinished work, missing evidence and checks nobody ran are not violations; do not withhold ok for them. If the input has "stop_hook_active": true, Claude was already sent back once this turn: answer {"ok": true}.
